author: Chris Pinson
title: Tanner Franklin brings the heat to Springfield - NewsBreak
text:
By Chris Pinson ,
1 hours ago
SPRINGFIELD--Springfield Cardinals starting pitcher, Tanner Franklin, puts the fast in fastball.
The 6'5, 225 lbs righthanded hurler can consistently make the ball turn into a blur, without breaking a sweat.
"I'd say for the most part, the entire game, I sit about 96, 98, 99," said Cardinals pitcher Tanner Franklin.
But when Franklin really wants to let loose, he can top out at 102 m.p.h. which makes it easy to understand why he's the 9th ranked overall prospect in the St. Louis Cardinals organization.
"I would say sometimes, when I'm really mad, and then, other times, I'm just trying to get that guy out of the box as fast as I can."
The unique thing about Franklin's style and mindset is it comes from his days as a relief pitcher, when he played for the Tennessee Volunteers, and his inspiration from old-school pitchers.
"When I was a reliever, it was hey, go in, throw as hard as you can, get these out as fast as you can. So I still kinda carry that mentality over into starting, but you gotta do it for longer. I love watching Nolan Ryan clips. I love those old school pitchers who weren't afraid to pitch inside, like Bob Gibson. He's gonna back you off the plate and make you respect it and make you be feared in the box and that's how I like to pitch."
Another major reason why Franklin idolizes the "Ryan Express" is because his father, Jim, played alongside Ryan, in the early 90s, at the Texas Rangers Spring Training. Franklin chuckled when he mentioned that and said "he's got some good stories."
Since joining Springfield on in early August, Franklin has put that flame throwing talent on display. In three starts, the Volunteers' alum is averaging 7 strikeouts a game.
Aside from pushing himself to be the best he can be, Franklin is also pushed the extra mile by current teammate and starting pitcher, Liam Doyle. Doyle and Franklin played for Tennessee their junior year, so getting to play on the same team, at the professional level, is like brothers reuniting.
"It's fun doing it in pro ball because we both have the same role now so we're pushing each other, helping each other out, cutting each other down whatever it takes to get the best out of each other so it's really fun to be around that guy."
